{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows negative sentiment (e.g., < 0.33) or recent low prices, indicating bearish momentum.",
    "Reduce forecast overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., > +10% from prior peak) by applying a dampening factor to avoid overreaction.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if price has deviated > ±15% from 15-day moving average, adjust forecast toward historical mean.",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to recent low prices (last 3-5 days) when sentiment is neutral or negative, to capture reversal potential.",
    "For horizon > 15 days, reduce forecast volatility by smoothing with 30-day moving average if sentiment is flat or negative.",
    "When sentiment history includes a recent positive spike (e.g., > 0.67), increase forecast confidence but cap upward adjustment to avoid overestimation.",
    "If true outcome consistently underperforms model (e.g., 3 consecutive days below forecast), reduce next forecast by 5-10% to account for model bias.",
    "For sentiment history with 0.33 or higher, allow moderate upward bias but cap at +10% above recent high to avoid overcorrection."
  ]
}
